```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width  = 7,
  fig.asp    = 0.618,
  out.width  = "90%",
  fig.align  = "center",
  dpi        = 150
)

library(SDR)
library(ggplot2)
```

This vignette demonstrates a basic comparison of the time complexity of the three functions: VSDRbias, VSDR.Gen, and VSDR.exp. The most optimized version is VSDR.Gen which is recommended for real-world use. VDR.exp is the most straightforwardly written but the slowest performer. 

```{r setup2, cache=TRUE}
H <- 25
parmlst <- list(
  Nh = rep(1000, H),
  nh = sample(5:10, H, replace=TRUE),
  muh = runif(H, min=1, max=10),
  sigmah = runif(H, min=1, max=2),
  alphah = runif(H, min=0.05, max=1)
)

nh_seq <- list(parmlst$nh, parmlst$nh*2, parmlst$nh*3, parmlst$nh*4)
results_list <- list()
```

We generate a random parameter list with `r H` strata then increase the sample size to 2, 3, and 4 times the original values.

```{r step1}
results_df <- data.frame(n=sapply(nh_seq, sum),
                         time=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         Vtru=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         EVSDR=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         RelBias=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)))

for(i in 1:length(nh_seq)){
  parmlst$nh <- nh_seq[[i]]
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  results <- VSDRbias(parmlst, PermArr)
  end_time <- Sys.time()
  results_df$time[i] <- end_time - start_time
  results_df$Vtru[i] <- results$Vtru
  results_df$EVSDR[i] <- results$EVSDR
  results_df$RelBias[i] <- results$RelBias
}
results_df$func <- "VSDRbias"

results_list[[length(results_list) + 1]] <- results_df
```

```{r step2, cache=TRUE}
results_df <- data.frame(n=sapply(nh_seq, sum),
                         time=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         Vtru=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         EVSDR=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         RelBias=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)))

for(i in 1:length(nh_seq)){
  parmlst$nh <- nh_seq[[i]]
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  results <- VSDR.exp(parmlst, PermArr)
  end_time <- Sys.time()
  results_df$time[i] <- end_time - start_time
  results_df$Vtru[i] <- results$Vtru
  results_df$EVSDR[i] <- results$EVSDR
  results_df$RelBias[i] <- results$RelBias
}
results_df$func <- "VSDR.exp"

results_list[[length(results_list) + 1]] <- results_df
```

```{r step3}
results_df <- data.frame(n=sapply(nh_seq, sum),
                         time=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         Vtru=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         EVSDR=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)),
                         RelBias=rep(NA, length=length(nh_seq)))

for(i in 1:length(nh_seq)){
  parmlst$nh <- nh_seq[[i]]
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  results <- VSDR.Gen(parmlst, PermArr)
  end_time <- Sys.time()
  results_df$time[i] <- end_time - start_time
  results_df$Vtru[i] <- results$Vtru
  results_df$EVSDR[i] <- results$EVSDR
  results_df$RelBias[i] <- results$RelBias
}
results_df$func <- "VSDR.Gen"

results_list[[length(results_list) + 1]] <- results_df
```

```{r compare}
results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
```

The graph below shows the comparison of the three functions on the same set of parameters. 
```{r graph, fig.cap="Time versus Total Sample Size by Function"}
ggplot(results, 
       aes(x=n, y=time, group=func, shape=func)
       ) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  xlab("Total Sample Size") + 
  ylab("Time (seconds)")
```

Finally, we show that the output values are all identical for all three functions.
```{r table}
results_to_print <- results[order(results$n, results$func), 
              c("n", "func", "Vtru", "EVSDR", "RelBias")]
rownames(results_to_print) <- NULL
num <- vapply(results_to_print, is.numeric, logical(1))
results_to_print[num] <- lapply(results_to_print[num], round, digits = 4)
print(results_to_print)
```
